key_insight: Cross-task parameter sharing can turn majority-vote self-reinforcement into a collective instability, driving reward toward one while accuracy collapses.
engineering_relevance: Scaling label-free RLVR to more training problems can increase collapse risk when shared amplification outpaces per-problem answer sharpening.
method: Derive a solvable many-problem model comparing shared-mode growth with per-problem sharpening.
Predict a critical dataset size governed by coupling strength, initial confidence, and perturbation size.
Test predictions in simulations and probe shared-direction effects in a small Transformer.
evidence_signal: Simulations support a sharp collapse transition and approximately inverse-square coupling dependence; small-Transformer experiments prevent collapse by removing the shared direction and restore it by reinstating that direction.
watch_item: Validation uses a simplified model and a small Transformer; applicability to larger models and practical stabilization methods needs further testing.
paper_title: Collective Dynamics of Self-Reinforcement: How Cross-Task Coupling Drives Policy Collapse in Unsupervised RLVR
